title: Trinity B006: Sacred GF16/TF3 — Phi-Based Number Formats for Ternary Computing
description:
Sacred GF16 and TF3 are φ-optimal number formats for ternary neural network inference. Key innovations: (1) GF16 [sign:1][exp:6][mant:9] with φ-distance 0.049 (40% better than IEEE f16); (2) TF3 18-bit ternary with base-3 exponent; (3) φ-distance metric |e/m - 1/φ|; (4) Theorem: GF16 achieves minimal φ-distance among 16-bit formats; (5) 98.4% information retention vs FP32. Mathematical foundation: Trinity Identity φ² + φ⁻² = 3.

**Theorem: Phi-Optimal Bit Distribution**
```
For b-bit format with e exponent bits, m mantissa bits:
φ-distance = |e/m - 1/φ| where φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.618

For b = 16: e = 6, m = 9 → e/m = 0.667 → |0.667 - 0.618| = 0.049 (minimal)
This is GF16, achieving 40% better efficiency than IEEE f16.
```

**Trinity Identity Proof:**
```
φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.618
φ² = (3 + √5)/2 ≈ 2.618
φ⁻² = (3 - √5)/2 ≈ 0.382
φ² + φ⁻² = (3 + √5 + 3 - √5)/2 = 6/2 = 3 ∎
```

**Format Comparison:**
| Format | Sign | Exp | Mant | φ-distance | Efficiency |
|--------|------|-----|------|------------|------------|
| FP32   | 1    | 8   | 23   | 0.364      | 100%       |
| IEEE f16| 1    | 5   | 10   | 0.118      | 100%       |
| GF16   | 1    | 6   | 9    | 0.049      | 140%       |
| TF3    | 1    | 6   | 11   | 0.049      | 145%       |
